summary: the mean of independent estimates of one quantity, their standard deviation and the standard error of the mean

inputs.name: estimates
inputs.meaning: independent estimates of one quantity, all in one unit: one per block of a run, per subset of particles, per replicate or per scan subset

outputs.name: mean
outputs.meaning: the mean of the estimates, in their unit

outputs.name: standard_deviation
outputs.meaning: the sample standard deviation, with n - 1

outputs.name: standard_error
outputs.meaning: the standard deviation over the square root of the number of estimates

validity: estimates that are independent of one another: blocks long beside the correlation time, or replicates from independent starts; with correlated estimates the standard error is too small

source.citation: A. Grossfield et al., Best Practices for Quantification of Uncertainty and Sampling Quality in Molecular Simulations, Living J. Comput. Mol. Sci. 1 (2018) 5067 (read 2026-11-17, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6286151/)
source.locus: Sec. 1.2.1, Eqs. 6 and 8: the sample standard deviation over n - 1 and the experimental standard deviation of the mean s(x)/sqrt(n), for estimates that are uncorrelated

note: The block-averaging section of the source (7.3.2) was read through a summary only; the relation used here is Eqs. 6 and 8, read verbatim. No value of the source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field. v2 is v1 made common, unchanged in its code and its cases' values: every simulation bundle carries it (the person, 2026-11-18, docs/ideas/20261118.md; meta_agent/tasks/025), and each worked case names the kind of system it is worked on, at least two unrelated kinds. A build adapts it to an engine as a next version that names the engine and says adapted_from.
